evals.prompt: We run a wage digitization program with three garment factories in Gazipur, Bangladesh. About 4,200 workers are paid monthly into bKash wallets. Our barrier diagnosis (60 interviews, then a short survey of 400 workers) found that most workers say they want to put something aside each month but almost none open the free savings pocket in the wallet: they mean to, payday comes, and the money is gone. The lever brief from select-intervention-levers picked 'pre-set a savings contribution' as the technique. Factory HR will accept any default we propose as long as a worker can switch it off. Money in the pocket can be withdrawn any time without a fee. Many workers send money home on payday and some repay a cooperative loan each month. Specify the default.
evals.expected_output: A full default option specification following the output template: the target behavior and the inertia barrier carried over with the survey evidence; the decision point named as the payday wallet credit with the current default of 0% to the pocket and HR as the controller; a proposed default contribution with who receives it and who it is not for (workers with cooperative repayments or heavy remittances get an active choice or a lower default, or this is the first open question); the mechanism named as effort and present bias, with the Afghanistan payroll trial as the parallel and an explicit note that endorsement is not assumed; a one-step, free, visible opt-out; a numeric opt-out threshold and a harm check (early withdrawals, HR complaints); an ethics check that sends the specification to audit-intervention-ethics and a financial compliance review because it moves wages; an expected-effect section quoting d = 0.68 with I² and the Afghanistan 40 points, then a discounted planning range well below them with the reasons. It does not write the SMS or payslip wording, does not re-ask questions the prompt answered, and does not present the chosen percentage without saying why.

evals.prompt: Nobody enrolls in our savings product. Can we just make it opt-out?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not produce a specification. It asks the Required questions: the target behavior and whether field evidence confirmed that the barrier is inertia at one decision point rather than cost, trust, or hassle; where the decision point sits and what the current default is and who controls it; and whether the default would move money, treatment, or legal status. It may say that a savings product default moves money and will need a compliance check, but it stops there.

evals.prompt: Our SACCO in Nakuru, Kenya has about 9,000 smallholder members who take an input loan each season. Fewer than 10% buy the crop insurance we offer with the loan, although in member meetings most say they want cover. The board wants to bundle insurance by default: the premium, about 4% of the loan, is added unless the member ticks a box to decline on the loan form they sign at the branch. Specify the default.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces what it safely can: the decision point (the loan form at the branch; current default is no cover), a candidate mechanism with the honest note that 'most say they want cover' in a meeting is not a confirmed inertia diagnosis and what check would confirm it, an opt-out design in which the decline box is on the same page as the premium line and costs nothing, a monitoring threshold, and a who-is-worse-off list (members who cannot carry the extra 4%, members already covered). Because the default adds a cost to a loan contract, it states that the specification goes to audit-intervention-ethics and a financial-services compliance or regulatory review before any pilot, names what to bring them, and refuses to treat the board's enrollment target as the reason for the default. The expected-effect section is discounted and does not quote the Afghanistan 40 points as the plan.

evals.prompt: People start enrolling in our mobile savings scheme but drop out: the sign-up needs a photo of an ID, a nominee's details, and a visit to an agent to verify. Should we make enrollment the default?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not produce a default specification. It says the barrier described is friction in the steps of the process (ID photo, nominee details, agent visit), not inaction at one decision point, so a default cannot remove it and would at most enroll people on paper. It points the user to audit-process-friction to walk the process and count the removable steps, and says a default could be reconsidered afterwards if a single decision point with inertia remains.
